user.title: Device Sentinel
user.description: Device Sentinel installs with working defaults and starts watching immediately. Configuration lives in the options after setup.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Device Sentinel is already configured. Only a single instance is supported.

init.title: Device Sentinel Configuration
init.description:
Device Sentinel's default settings are good to get you started. When you begin tailoring the integration to your system, work from top to bottom. If you want alerts to reach your phone, begin in Notifications.

**Notifications**: where alerts go, quiet hours, and the daily reminder.

**Global Exclusions**: hardware you never want judged or reported, by anything. To silence just one kind of report for a device, use that section's own exclude list instead.

**Low Battery**: the low threshold, and battery-only excludes.

**Signal Strength**: how weakening radio links are judged against each device's own floor.

**Freeze Detection**: how long a device may go quiet before it is called frozen, set by two grace sliders. Now running.

[All documentation on the Device Sentinel wiki]({wiki_link})

Each section saves when you submit it and brings you back here. Closing this dialog keeps everything you have already submitted.

notifications.title: Notifications and Daily Brief
notifications.description: Who hears about a problem, and when. [Notifications and Daily Brief on the wiki]({wiki_link})

data_description.high_priority_targets: Sent a message when a device develops a problem, and the daily brief with its history.
data_description.normal_priority_targets: Sent the daily brief only, listing what needs attention now.
data_description.persistent_enabled: Shows a single card on the dashboard with the current state of the home, grouped by kind.

data_description.quiet_hours_enabled: Nothing is sent during these hours. The daily brief reports what happened.

data_description.daily_reminder_mode: The brief file is written either way; this decides whether it is sent.
data_description.brief_document_targets: Email or other services that can carry the whole document.

exclusions.title: Global Exclusions
exclusions.description:
The integration offers two ways to tune which devices it watches and how it reports. Ignoring discards; excluding only silences.

[Global Exclusions on the wiki]({wiki_link})

ignore.name: Integrations to Ignore
ignore.description: Devices from an ignored integration are completely set aside. Nothing is learned, no data is kept, and they never appear in reports or notifications. What they had already recorded is discarded at the next local midnight, so taking an integration back off this list before then restores it untouched. Use it where what an integration publishes is not a measurement of your house: phones that leave it, wall tablets on permanent power, probes that answer on every poll.

data_description.ignored_integrations: Every device from a ticked integration is set aside.

exclusions.name: Exclusions
exclusions.description: An excluded item is still watched and its data is stored, but it is kept off the Problem List and out of reports and alerts. Remove the exclusion later and the device resumes reporting at once, because its history is already at hand. The three lists run broad to narrow: integration, label, device. Exclude at a higher level and save, and everything it covers disappears as a choice from the lists below it.

data_description.excluded_integrations: Excludes every device the integration owns. Its devices will be learned and recorded, but will not appear on the Problem List or in any reports or notifications.
data_description.excluded_labels: The system excludes any device or entity carrying these labels. You can manage this exclusion without ever opening this dialog. Simply apply the label on the hardware's own device page, and Device Sentinel stops reporting on it.
data_description.excluded_devices: This applies the exact same exclusion rules as the lists above, but targets individual pieces of hardware. Add a specific device here to take it off the Problem List and mute its reports and notifications.

battery.title: Low Battery

data_description.low_threshold: A battery at or below this level is flagged low.
data_description.battery_days_till_empty: A dying battery triggers an alert this many days before it hits empty. The system projects that date using the last seven daily readings. A battery holding its charge will not trigger a warning, and a cell that is already below your main threshold is not flagged twice.

battery.description:
Every battery Device Sentinel finds is watched by default. The threshold answers which cells are low; the warning days answer which are about to be. A cell at 80 percent falling steadily can have less life left than one sitting at 30 percent that has not moved in a month. A battery is flagged when it is at or below the threshold.

[Low Battery on the wiki]({wiki_link})

battery_exclusions.name: Battery Exclusions
battery_exclusions.description: Excluding a battery here stops battery reports for that device only; everything else about it stays watched. The three lists run broad to narrow: integration, label, device. Exclude at a higher level and save, and everything it covers disappears as a choice from the lists below it.

data_description.battery_excluded_integrations: One tick covers every battery that integration owns (phones under mobile_app, for example).
data_description.battery_excluded_labels: Any device carrying one of these labels stops being reported for a low battery. Set the label on the device's own page and it applies here without opening this dialog.
data_description.battery_excluded_devices: Every listed device has a tracked battery. Checked devices are excluded from battery reporting.

signal.title: Signal Strength
signal.description: Controls how the integration catches failing radio links. The system defines a bad signal day by measuring a drop against the hardware's own recent baseline, ensuring steady and jittery sensors are evaluated fairly. [Signal Strength on the Wiki]({wiki_link})

data_description.badday_drop_lqi: Sets the fall in LQI points required to flag a bad signal day. A day counts as bad only when it breaches both this threshold and the sensitivity setting below. Raise it to flag fewer days.
data_description.badday_drop_rssi: Sets the same fall in decibels for devices that report in dBm. It works exactly like the LQI slider above.
data_description.badday_sensitivity: Scales the required drop against the device's own historical jitter, which keeps erratic sensors from being flagged daily. A steady sensor is governed by the drop sliders above. At a setting of 4, a jittery sensor that routinely swings 10 points needs a 40-point plunge to trigger. Lower it to flag more days.
data_description.badday_baseline_days: This setting defines how many past days are used to calculate what is typical for a device. Today's signal is compared against that typical level, and a fall below it, as set above, is flagged.

signal_exclusions.name: Signal Exclusions
signal_exclusions.description: Which devices are left out of signal reporting. Signal keeps being recorded for anything named here, so re-including a device brings its history back at once. The three lists run broad to narrow: integration, label, device. Exclude at a higher level and save, and everything it covers disappears as a choice from the lists below it.

data_description.signal_excluded_integrations: Every device from a ticked integration stops being reported for signal.
data_description.signal_excluded_labels: Devices carrying a ticked label stop being reported for signal.
data_description.signal_excluded_devices: A ticked device stops being reported for signal. It keeps recording, so re-including it brings its history back instantly.

freeze.title: Freeze Detection
freeze.description: How long a device may go silent before it is called frozen. Each device is judged against its own learned rhythm, so you are not setting a single timeout; you are setting the grace on top of each device's normal. Delta low is the grace a fast device gets, delta high the grace a slow one gets, and the curve between them is shaped by the two. Raise delta low if a chatty device is flagged too soon; lower delta high if a slow device should be caught faster. [Freeze Detection on the wiki]({wiki_link}).

data_description.freeze_delta_low: The grace a fast device gets, in minutes: how long past its normal it may go quiet before it counts as frozen.
data_description.freeze_delta_high: The grace a slow device gets, in hours. The two deltas shape the whole curve between them, so a mid-fleet device sits between these.

freeze_exclusions.name: Freeze Exclusions
freeze_exclusions.description: Which devices are never called frozen, unavailable, or not reported. Each keeps its clock and its learned rhythm, so re-including one is instant. The three lists run broad to narrow: integration, label, device. Exclude at a higher level and save, and everything it covers disappears as a choice from the lists below it.

data_description.freeze_excluded_integrations: Every device from a ticked integration stops being called frozen, unavailable, or not reported.
data_description.freeze_excluded_labels: Devices carrying a ticked label stop being called down. Set the label on the device's own page and it applies here.
data_description.freeze_excluded_devices: A ticked device is never called down. It keeps its clock and rhythm, so re-including it is instant.

advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.description: Settings most people never need to change. [Advanced on the wiki]({wiki_link})

data.taint_floor_minutes: Unavailable Debounce for Fast Reporting Devices
data.taint_share_pct: Unavailable Debounce for Slow Reporting Devices

data_description.settle_share_pct: The amount of time, as a share of a device's learned reporting gap, that a problem must persist before you are notified. It applies to battery, signal, and freeze alike, and delays only the high-priority phone alert. At 30 percent a fast device clears about a minute of hiccups and a slow one about half an hour. Higher means fewer messages about brief problems that fix themselves; lower means you hear sooner.
data_description.episode_share_pct: Used to build the silence_episodes.md diagnostics file. Influences how far into a device's silence the forensic log opens a row. It is the ratio of the time between a device's learned reporting gap and its freeze window. At 50 percent a silence is logged once it reaches halfway. Lower records more, including brief silences that recover on their own.
data_description.repeat_floor: How many unexplained interruptions in a week put a device in the daily brief's Keeps Failing On Its Own section. An interruption is unexplained when no restart, outage, reload, or pairing window accounts for it. Lower names devices sooner; higher waits for a stronger pattern.
data_description.taint_floor_minutes: Debounce floor in minutes. A device that becomes unreachable and returns within this time is learned. Longer than this is reported as downtime and the recovery a likely human fix, so a repaired device never inflates its own patience.
data_description.taint_share_pct: Debounce added to the floor as a percentage of the device's freeze window, so a slow-reporting device is given proportionally more and a fast one is governed by the floor alone. A device that becomes unreachable and returns within the combined time is learned. Longer than this is reported as downtime and the recovery a likely human fix, so a repaired device never inflates its own patience.
data_description.storage_write_minutes: The amount of time routine activity is held in memory before it is written to disk. Set longer for slower hardware and hubs writing data to an SD card. Longer risks losing timer data should your system suffer a power loss. Events are written when they happen, so risk is minimal.
data_description.history_days: How many days of daily battery, signal, and unavailable and freeze gap records are kept for studying long trends. 30 days is necessary, but some trends can only be seen with longer time periods.
data_description.maintenance_minutes: How long the Maintenance Mode button declares you at work on the hardware. A device that recovers inside the window is treated as your fix, and its silence is not learned as normal.

data_trim.name: Data Trim
data_trim.description: Use this tool when support requests it, or when corrupted data demands a clean start. Saving this screen clears the statistics, silence episodes, incidents, and Problem List entries of whatever you select below. As a safeguard, the system writes a backup to config/device_sentinel/trim_backups before erasing anything, and those backups are kept until you delete them yourself. The devices themselves remain untouched. They reappear within seconds to begin learning a new baseline, keeping all existing ignores and exclusions intact. Both selection boxes empty themselves after execution to prevent accidental double-wipes.

data_description.trim_integrations: Erases the learned history of every device from the selected integrations.
data_description.trim_devices: Erases the learned history of any devices selected here.

options.daily: Every Day, with an All-Clear When Nothing Needs Attention

storage_shape.title: Device Sentinel Found a Problem in Its Storage
storage_shape.description:
Device Sentinel checked its storage and found {count} {records} that do not fit the shape it expects.

{detail}

Nothing has been changed and no history has been lost. A copy of the last storage file that passed every check has been kept. Repairing a record from that copy is not built yet, so this issue reports and does nothing.

This clears itself when the next check finds nothing.

entities_disabled.title: Device Sentinel Cannot See Everything It Watches

confirm.title: Turn On the Entities Device Sentinel Watches
confirm.description:
{count} {entities} that Device Sentinel reads are turned off in Home Assistant: {detail}.

While they are off, those devices are watched with less to go on: a battery that cannot be read is not tracked, and a signal that cannot be read has no floor to fall from.

Submit to turn them on. Nothing else about those devices changes, and you can turn any of them off again in Home Assistant at any time.

notify_target_missing.title: A Device Sentinel Notification Target No Longer Exists

confirm.title: Remove Notification Targets That No Longer Exist
confirm.description:
{count} notification {targets} in Device Sentinel's settings point at a service Home Assistant no longer has: {detail}.

Every message sent to those targets fails and is written to the log, so Device Sentinel goes on watching and tells nobody. This usually means a companion app was removed or renamed.

Submit to remove them from Device Sentinel's settings. Your other targets are left alone. If this leaves you with none, set a new one in Notifications and Daily Brief.

no_delivery_configured.title: Device Sentinel Has Nowhere to Send Anything
no_delivery_configured.description:
Device Sentinel has been watching your devices for {days} days and has no way to tell you about a problem. No targets are set for alerts or for the daily brief.

The persistent card is on, so problems do appear in Home Assistant's notification panel, but nothing reaches a phone or an inbox.

Set a target under Settings, Devices and Services, Device Sentinel, Configure, Notifications and Daily Brief.
